outcome: No event since 26 January 2024 proves, disproves, or bounds the number of quadrisecants of a wild knot; the conjecture is still listed as open on Wikipedia, and the only post-2024 wild-knot papers I opened do not address quadrisecants. The conjecture originates in Kuperberg's 1994 paper, where it is stated for wild arcs in R^3 rather than wild knots.
problem_asks: One conjectured claim, universal over a class. (1) The class: wild knots (closed curves that are not tame; Kuperberg's setting is R^3, the statement does not name the ambient space). (2) The quantity: quadrisecants, meaning straight lines meeting the knot in four points. (3) The claim: every wild knot has infinitely many quadrisecants (asserted as a conjecture, with 'always' in the Wikipedia wording and 'Does every wild knot have infinitely many quadrisecants?' in the unsolved-problem box). Nothing is asked about bounds, about finiteness for particular wild knots, or about tame knots, which are known to have quadrisecants.

events.what_happened: Greg Kuperberg, 'Quadrisecants of knots and links', J. Knot Theory Ramifications 3 (1994) 41-50; arXiv math/9712205 (v1 1 Dec 1997, v2 25 Jun 2002). The paper proves that every non-trivial tame knot or link in R^3 has four collinear points (Theorem I.3, Theorem V.3). In its open-questions section (Section VI) it states Conjecture VI.4: 'Every wild arc in R^3 has infinitely many quadrisecants.' This is the origin of the wild-knot version cited on Wikipedia (the Wild knot article cites Kuperberg 1994 for 'every wild knot has an infinite number of quadrisecants'). The text I read is the arXiv v2 rendering on ar5iv; I did not read the 1994 print version or the v1 text.
events.revisions: arXiv math/9712205 v1 1 Dec 1997; v2 25 Jun 2002 (current). The journal date 1994 comes from the citation on Wikipedia and in search results; the exact month was not confirmed.
events.delivers: Conjecture only. Establishes no quadrisecant count for any wild object. The theorem it proves covers tame knots and links only. The conjecture it poses is about wild ARCS in R^3, not wild knots.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The infinitude claim for wild knots is posed here, not established. Whether the wild-arc form implies the wild-knot form is a scope question for the judging pass; the Wikipedia wild-knot article states that every closed curve containing a wild arc is a wild knot, but I did not confirm that sentence on the page itself.

checked_by.qualification: A refereed research journal in knot theory
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 1994. Publication does not endorse the conjecture in Section VI; no separate referee report on Conjecture VI.4 is public.

events.time_since_posted: About 32 years since the 1994 publication (about 29 years since the 1997 arXiv posting). I found no public resolution, refutation, or dedicated discussion of Conjecture VI.4 in the sources I read.
events.doubts: Scope mismatch rather than doubt about the result: the conjecture as stated by its author concerns wild arcs; the Wikipedia list and wild-knot article state it for wild knots. Nothing I read disputes the conjecture itself.
events.direction: Asserts infinitude of quadrisecants for wild arcs in R^3. This cuts the same way as the problem's claim (infinitely many), but it is a conjecture, not a result.

events.what_happened: Sheng Bai, Chao Wang, Jiajun Wang, 'Counterexamples to the quadrisecant approximation conjecture', arXiv 1605.00538 (journal version reported as J. Knot Theory Ramifications, 2018; not opened). Disproves the quadrisecant approximation conjecture: every knot type contains two knots, the quadrisecant approximation of one has self-intersections and that of the other is a knot of a different type. It concerns knots with finitely many quadrisecants.
events.revisions: arXiv 1605.00538. Month taken from the arXiv identifier; the submission page itself was not read for a date. Journal year 2018 from search results only.
events.delivers: Establishes that the quadrisecant approximation of certain knots need not preserve knot type. A different question: it does not count, bound, or prove the infinitude of quadrisecants for any knot, wild or tame.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The paper does not address wild knots.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed research journal in knot theory

events.direction: Disproves a different conjecture (approximation preserves knot type). Does not cut for or against the quadrisecant-infinitude claim. The paper assumes finitely many quadrisecants and does not discuss the infinite case, except to quote Kuperberg's tame-knot result.
events.object: Pairs of knots within each knot type, one whose quadrisecant approximation self-intersects and one whose approximation has a different knot type. Constructed explicitly in the paper (not checked in detail here). Concerns finitely-many-quadrisecant knots.

events.what_happened: Sergey A. Melikhov, 'Is every knot isotopic to the unknot?', arXiv 2406.09365 (math.GT). Shows that the Bing sling is not isotopic to any PL knot, addressing Rolfsen's 1974 question. The paper calls the Bing sling 'R. H. Bing's example of a wild knot' (Section 1). No quadrisecant content: the word does not occur in the portions I read.
events.delivers: Establishes that one wild knot (the Bing sling) is not isotopic to a PL knot. Nothing about quadrisecants of any wild knot.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The paper does not touch the quadrisecant count.
events.time_since_posted: About 28 months. I did not search for reviews of this paper specifically; no engagement with the quadrisecant question was found.
events.direction: Does not cut for or against the infinitude claim; it is a classification-type result about wild knots.

events.what_happened: Juan Pablo Diaz, Gabriela Hinojosa, Alberto Verjovsky, 'N-dimensional beaded necklaces and higher dimensional wild knots, invariant by a Schottky group', arXiv 2410.15183. Builds wild knots in S^(n+2) with a Cantor set of wild points from a smooth n-dimensional knot, using a conformal Schottky group; shows fiberedness is preserved. Higher-dimensional and not about quadrisecants.
events.revisions: v1 19 Oct 2024; a v2 exists (HTML v2 listed in search results, date not read).
events.delivers: Constructs higher-dimensional wild knots with controlled wild points. Nothing about quadrisecants, lines, or their count.
events.time_since_posted: About 24 months; no engagement with the quadrisecant question found.
events.direction: Does not cut for or against the infinitude claim. Different setting (n-dimensional knots in S^(n+2)).
events.object: A wild n-dimensional knot with a Cantor set of wild points, built from a smooth knot and a beaded necklace subordinate to it using inversions in bounding spheres of a Schottky group. Explicit construction; not a counterexample to anything here.

events.what_happened: Gabriela Hinojosa, Ulises Morales-Fuentes, Rogelio Valdez, Alberto Verjovsky, 'Wild knots embedded in the Menger Sponge', arXiv 2602.20384. Gives explicit recursive constructions of infinitely many non-equivalent wild knots inside the Menger sponge, with wild points in a standard Cantor set. No quadrisecant content in the abstract, introduction, or the visible text of the HTML version.
events.revisions: v1 23 Feb 2026; the abstract page shows v3 revised 6 Sep 2026.
events.delivers: Infinitely many non-equivalent wild knots in the Menger sponge. Nothing about quadrisecants.
events.time_since_posted: About 8 months; no engagement with the quadrisecant question found.
events.direction: Does not cut for or against the infinitude claim. Constructs wild knots; does not count their quadrisecants.
events.object: Explicit recursive family of wild knots in the Menger sponge, with wild points in a tame Cantor set (from the abstract). Not checked beyond the abstract and the visible HTML portion.

events.what_happened: Mary Y. Deng, Allison K. Henrich, Sean H. Kawano, Andrew R. Tawfeek, 'Taming Wild Knots with Mosaics', arXiv 2605.14185 (math.GT). Extends the Lomonaco-Kauffman knot-mosaic framework to a substantial subclass of wild knots with isolated wild points, using infinite rooted trees. No quadrisecant content in the portion of the HTML read.
events.delivers: A combinatorial representation of a subclass of wild knots. Nothing about quadrisecants.
events.time_since_posted: About 5 months; no engagement with the quadrisecant question found.
events.direction: Does not cut for or against the infinitude claim. Represents wild knots combinatorially; does not count quadrisecants.

events.what_happened: A Lean 4 benchmark statement on the lean-eval site, 'Pannwitz-Kuperberg quadrisecant theorem' (Lean name smooth_knot_has_quadrisecant): every smooth knot that is not the unknot has a quadrisecant. The problem page is undated and shows 'declaration uses sorry' next to 'All goals completed'; it gives no status line or 'Solved by' field, and 'Informal solution: Unavailable'. A search snippet reported a submitter (Kim Morrison) that the fetched page does not show. A search snippet also reported that the lean-eval leaderboard (legacy page) lists Axiom Prover (Axiom Math) with 207 problems solved and this row; I could not open that page (size limit) and the main eval page was still loading. Whether this problem is among Axiom's solved entries is unverified.
events.delivers: If proved, a formal version of the smooth-knot existence theorem (Pannwitz 1933 for polygons, Morton-Mond 1982 for smooth, Kuperberg 1994 for tame). It concerns smooth, not wild, knots.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the wild-knot infinitude claim is untouched.
events.time_since_posted: Undated. No human commentary on the Lean row found.
events.doubts: Status conflict on the problem page: 'declaration uses sorry' alongside 'All goals completed!'. The 'Not yet solved' status came from an earlier search snippet, and the leaderboard row (Axiom Prover, 207 solved) came from another snippet that I could not open. The two sources cannot both be current. Mathlib has no knot theory per the page, so a proof would have to build that setting.
events.direction: Concerns the smooth (tame) case, which the existing literature already establishes. A proof would agree with known results and says nothing about wild knots.

disputes.summary: The conjecture is stated for wild arcs in R^3 by its author (Kuperberg, Conjecture VI.4, 1994/1997), but for wild knots on the Wikipedia list and the wild-knot article, which cite Kuperberg for it. Whether the two are the same claim is unresolved.

The Wikipedia quadrisecant article credits the quadrisecant approximation conjecture to Kim, while Bai-Wang-Wang (2016) credits it to Jin. This concerns the approximation conjecture, not the wild-knot problem, and is recorded for completeness.

summary: Nothing I found since 26 January 2024 proves, disproves, or bounds the number of quadrisecants of a wild knot or wild arc. The Wikipedia list still records the conjecture under Topology as open, and the Wikipedia quadrisecant article cites Kuperberg (1994) for it. The conjecture originates in Kuperberg's 'Quadrisecants of knots and links' (JKTR 1994; arXiv math/9712205), where I read it on the ar5iv rendering of v2 (2002): 'Conjecture VI.4: Every wild arc in R^3 has infinitely many quadrisecants.' That is a wild-arc statement; the list and wild-knot article state the wild-knot version, and I have not resolved whether they are the same claim. Kuperberg's main theorem covers tame knots and links only. Denne's 2016 survey (checked on ar5iv) does not mention the wild conjecture; its open problem is bounding quadrisecant counts for a knot type. Bai-Wang-Wang (2016, arXiv 1605.00538) disproves the quadrisecant approximation conjecture, a different question, and assumes finiteness. The post-2024 wild-knot preprints I opened (Melikhov 2024 on the Bing sling; Diaz-Hinojosa-Verjovsky 2024 on higher-dimensional wild knots; Hinojosa et al. 2026 on wild knots in the Menger sponge; Deng et al. 2026 on mosaics for wild knots) classify or construct wild knots, and none mentions quadrisecants in the text I read. None is a candidate for this problem. For AI: no system is credited with anything on this problem. Searches for AI involvement (AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, GPT, Claude, Gemini, erdosproblems-style trackers, knot-theory AI work) returned only unrelated knot results: the 2021 DeepMind Nature knot-invariant paper, a 2026 Lipshitz-Sarkar preprint about a ChatGPT model on Khovanov homology, and a 2026 lecture-notes paper on a knot inequality. None of these concerns quadrisecants, and I did not open the last two. The one lead near this problem is the lean-eval row for the Pannwitz-Kuperberg smooth-knot theorem, whose status is contradictory across my sources: the page shows 'declaration uses sorry' and 'All goals completed', and a search snippet gives a leaderboard row for Axiom Prover (207 solved) that I could not open. That row concerns the smooth case, not wild knots, so it bears on this bullet only by being recorded. Close calls: (a) whether the wild-arc conjecture counts for the wild-knot bullet, which the judging pass must decide; (b) whether the lean-eval row names an AI system on this result, which I could not verify; I left systems empty rather than assert it.
competing_reading: Read the sources together and the wild-knot bullet is the same conjecture as Kuperberg's wild-arc Conjecture VI.4, so any resolution of the wild-arc form would settle it. Read them separately and the wild-knot claim is only what Wikipedia says it is, with no published wild-knot version from its origin, so nothing has happened. On the AI side, one could read the lean-eval leaderboard snippet as an AI system closing a related formal theorem; I did not confirm that row, and it concerns the smooth case in any reading.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The 1994 JKTR print version and the 1997 v1 text of math/9712205, to confirm the exact wording of the conjecture and whether it is stated for wild knots anywhere. The 1989 sci.math post by Kuperberg (a search snippet, not opened) may be where the wild-knot form originated. (2) An arXiv math.GT and MathSciNet/zbMATH search for 'quadrisecant' combined with 'wild', from 2024 to the present. My search tool cannot browse arXiv listings by date, so this is the main unsearched gap. (3) The live lean-eval leaderboard row and problem-page history for smooth_knot_has_quadrisecant (solver, date, sorry status). (4) Whether a wild arc with finitely many quadrisecants exists, or a published proof that wild knots reduce to wild arcs in this sense.
